conceptual assets.information: The enable setting controls whether the SDI FIFOs are cleared and whether serial processing is enabled; the IP behavior depends on it. It is written through the bus control access and can be read back.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because an unchecked bus write changes the setting at line 133; availability is at risk because the setting clears both FIFOs at lines 200 and 239 and controls serial state at line 296.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker issuing a control-register write could disable the interface, clear queued data, or prevent serial transfers.

conceptual assets.information: The payload written by the bus is queued for transmission and shifted onto the SDI data output. The serial transmit function depends on preserving and delivering this payload.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because the payload reaches the observable serial output at line 345; integrity is at risk because bus data is loaded into the transmit path at line 201 and shifted through the serial register at lines 305 and 327; availability is at risk because disabling the interface clears the transmit FIFO at line 200 and sampled chip select controls whether transmission starts at line 307.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter a bus write, clear the transmit queue, or prevent the selected payload from being transmitted.

conceptual assets.information: The payload sampled from the SDI data input is assembled into a serial word, buffered, and returned to the bus. The receive function depends on capturing and making the received word available for software.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because the received payload can be exposed through the bus response at line 162; integrity is at risk because sampled input data enters at line 270 and is assembled by serial-register updates at line 327; availability is at risk because receive data can be discarded when the receive FIFO is cleared at line 239 or when chip select terminates the transfer at line 324.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter sampled serial bits, clear the receive buffer, or terminate reception before the word is returned.

conceptual assets.information: The chip-select handshake frames SDI transfers and determines whether serial reception or transmission starts, continues, or terminates. It enters through sdi_csn_i and is consumed by the unit without a corresponding output port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Availability is at risk because the sampled chip-select controls transfer start at line 307 and causes the serial engine to leave its transfer states at lines 315 and 324.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could hold or toggle chip select to prevent a transfer or truncate it before completion.

conceptual assets.information: The interrupt notification reports selected receive or transmit FIFO conditions to the surrounding system. The IP or its software service path depends on this notification to respond to pending serial activity.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because the notification is produced by the internal condition logic at line 249 and can therefore be asserted or suppressed incorrectly; availability is at risk because reset and the same condition logic can withhold the interrupt at lines 247 and 249.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could cause false interrupt indications or suppress the notification so pending receive or transmit work is not serviced.

considered, not kept.reason: These bus-written settings only tune the interrupt-request output, so the Port options rule bars them as concepts of their own; their use is in the interrupt expression at lines 249 through 254.
The serial clock input only paces sampling and state advancement at lines 268, 317, and 326, so the Clocks and resets rule excludes it as a conceptual asset.
clk_i and rstn_i only time or reset internal logic and FIFO instances at lines 115, 123, 184, 185, 219, and 220, so the Clocks and resets rule excludes them.

The request strobe, direction, and address only select register or FIFO accesses and generate their strobes at lines 130 through 142, 202, and 240, so Access command fields and Forwarded transactions bar them as separate concepts.
The acknowledge repeats the request strobe and the error is tied to a constant at lines 125 and 126, so Bus handshake copies bars them as information of their own.

The FIFO availability, half-full, free, and empty indications only report or time buffered data and are returned or used in interrupt generation at lines 153 through 158 and 250 through 254, so Buffer and engine status bits bars a separate concept.

The serial state, count, start, done, and synchronizer stages only order or pace the serial payload transfer in the state machine at lines 297 through 340, so Sequencing state, Pacing pulses, and Working values exclude them.
RTX_FIFO fixes FIFO depth at build time through the generic and instance maps at lines 20, 176, and 211, so Build-time values excludes it from runtime conceptual assets.

reply keys: the 2026-10-13 format as written in 'raw'; 'reply' holds it in v5 keys
